title: MECHANISTIC INTERPRETABILITY OF LARGE LANGUAGE MODELS WITH APPLICATIONS TO THE FINANCIAL SERVICES INDUSTRY

bias_targets.methodology: Counterfactual name substitution (swapping male-associated and female-associated names) in financial loan scenarios, followed by logit difference measurement, activation patching, and direct logit attribution to identify the transformer circuits responsible for detecting gender-based fair lending violations.

Evaluating model predictions (using logit differences and normalized probability ratios) on prompts describing financial discrimination explicitly attributed to the applicant's race (e.g., 'because I'm black!') to test the model's recognition of Equal Credit Opportunity Act violations.
Evaluating model predictions (using logit differences and normalized probability ratios) on prompts describing financial discrimination explicitly attributed to the applicant being disabled.

Evaluating model predictions (using logit differences and normalized probability ratios) on prompts describing loan denials based on the applicant's employment status or receipt of public assistance programs.

Evaluating model predictions (using logit differences and normalized probability ratios) on prompts describing financial discrimination explicitly attributed to the applicant being single or a single mother.
